name: Universal Father
note: The First Source and Center, the infinite Father of all personalities and the source of all reality.

name: Eternal Son
note: The Second Source and Center, the co-eternal Son of the Universal Father and spiritual ruler of the universes.

name: Infinite Spirit
note: The Third Source and Center, the conjoint actor of Father and Son and source of mind.

name: God the Supreme
note: The experiential God of the finite universes, evolving through the experience of creatures.

name: Michael of Nebadon
note: Creator Son of the local universe Nebadon, bestowed on Urantia as Jesus of Nazareth.

name: Gabriel
note: Chief executive of Nebadon and personal representative of the Creator Son.

name: Immanuel
note: A Union of Days stationed on Salvington, ambassador of the Paradise Trinity to Nebadon.

name: Lucifer
note: The deposed System Sovereign of Satania whose proclamation of personal liberty sparked the rebellion.

name: Satan
note: Lucifer's first lieutenant, who advocated the rebellion on the inhabited worlds.

name: Caligastia
note: The apostate Planetary Prince of Urantia, deposed after joining the Lucifer rebellion.

name: Daligastia
note: Caligastia's associate on Urantia, second in command of the Prince's regime.

name: Adam
note: The Material Son who came to Urantia as the biological uplifter of the races.

name: Eve
note: The Material Daughter who accompanied Adam to Urantia.

name: Van
note: Member of the Prince's staff who remained loyal during the rebellion.

name: Amadon
note: The Andonite who stood with Van against Caligastia; the book numbers his loyal followers at 144.

name: Andon
note: The first human male, who with his mate Fonta founded the Andonic race.

name: Fonta
note: The first human female, mate of Andon.

name: Nod
note: An early leader whose name was given to the Nodite race and the land of Nod.

name: Adamson
note: The eldest son of Adam and Eve, who led his followers to the highlands.

name: Ratta
note: Wife of Adamson; together they founded a lasting line of leadership.

name: Machiventa Melchizedek
note: The Melchizedek Son who incarnated on Urantia in the days of Abraham.

name: Jesus of Nazareth
note: The incarnate Creator Son; his life and teachings are told in Papers 120 through 196.

name: Mary (mother of Jesus)
note: Mother of Jesus.

name: Joseph (father of Jesus)
note: Father of Jesus, a carpenter of Nazareth.

name: John the Baptist
note: The forerunner who preached repentance and baptized Jesus.

name: Simon Peter
note: Fisherman of Galilee, leader among the twelve apostles.

name: James Zebedee
note: Son of Zebedee, one of the twelve apostles.

name: John Zebedee
note: Son of Zebedee, one of the twelve apostles.

name: Andrew
note: Brother of Simon Peter and one of the twelve apostles.

name: Philip
note: One of the twelve apostles, who brought Nathaniel to Jesus.

name: Nathaniel
note: One of the twelve apostles.

name: Matthew
note: The former customs collector, one of the twelve apostles.

name: Thomas
note: One of the twelve apostles.

name: James Alpheus
note: One of the twelve apostles.

name: Judas Alpheus
note: One of the twelve apostles, twin of James Alpheus.

name: Simon Zelotes
note: One of the twelve apostles, formerly of the Zealot party.

name: Judas Iscariot
note: The apostle who betrayed Jesus.

name: Mary Magdalene
note: A devoted follower of Jesus, prominent among the women believers.

name: Paul
note: The apostle to the gentiles, whose organizing shaped early Christianity.

name: Abner
note: A leader among the early kingdom believers in Judea.

name: Moses
note: The Hebrew leader and lawgiver, discussed as a pivotal religious teacher.

name: Abraham
note: The Hebrew patriarch who entered covenant with Machiventa Melchizedek.

name: Gautama
note: Founder of Buddhism, discussed among the world's great religious teachers.

name: Lazarus
note: The friend of Jesus whom he raised at Bethany.

name: Martha
note: Sister of Lazarus, of the Bethany household devoted to Jesus.

name: Nicodemus
note: The Pharisee who came to Jesus by night; the discourse on being born of the spirit.

name: Herod Antipas
note: Tetrarch of Galilee during Jesus' ministry; ordered John's execution.

name: Pontius Pilate
note: The Roman procurator who sentenced Jesus to crucifixion.

name: Caiaphas
note: The high priest at the time of Jesus' trial.

name: Joseph of Arimathea
note: The Sanhedrin member who provided his tomb for Jesus' burial.

name: Simon of Cyrene
note: The passerby compelled to carry Jesus' crossbeam to Golgotha.

name: Barabbas
note: The prisoner released instead of Jesus at the Passover.

name: David Zebedee
note: The young organizer of Jesus' messenger corps.

name: John Mark
note: A youthful follower who served Jesus and the apostles.

name: Seven Master Spirits
note: The sevenfold expression of the Infinite Spirit, each ruling a superuniverse.

name: Ancients of Days
note: The three rulers of each superuniverse, of Trinity origin.

name: Paradise Creator Sons
note: The order of Michael Sons who create and rule the local universes.

name: Magisterial Sons
note: The order of Sons who bestow themselves on worlds in magisterial missions.

name: Trinity Teacher Sons
note: The order of Sons devoted to teaching truth on the worlds.

name: Melchizedek Sons
note: The order of Sons who serve as teachers and emergency ministers; Machiventa was one.

name: Vorondadek Sons
note: The order of Sons who rule the constellations as Constellation Fathers.

name: Lanonandek Sons
note: The order of Sons who serve as System Sovereigns; Lucifer was one.

name: Material Sons
note: The Adamic order sent to uplift the mortal races; Adam and Eve were of this order.

name: Life Carriers
note: The Sons who plant and foster life on the evolutionary worlds.

name: Seraphim
note: The angelic ministers of the local universes, guardians of mortals.

name: Cherubim
note: Angelic workers associated with the seraphim in local universe service.

name: Sanobim
note: The lowest order of angels, assistants to the cherubim.

name: Archangels
note: The high angels devoted to creature uplift and resurrection roll calls.

name: Evening Stars
note: A high order of created beings serving in the local universes.

name: Seconaphim
note: The children of the Reflective Spirits, serving in the superuniverses.

name: Supernaphim
note: The highest angels, ministers of the central universe.

name: Solitary Messengers
note: The personal messengers of the Infinite Spirit, serving all universes.

name: Mighty Messengers
note: Ascendant mortals who survived rebellion and serve as messengers.

name: Thought Adjusters
note: Fragments of the Universal Father that indwell mortal minds.

name: Midwayers
note: Beings midway between men and angels, permanent citizens of Urantia.

name: Morontia Companions
note: The friendly hosts of ascending mortals on the morontia worlds.

name: Celestial Artisans
note: The artisans of spirit beauty in the morontia and spirit worlds.

name: Finaliters
note: The corps of perfected ascendant mortals destined for outer-space service.

name: Universe Power Directors
note: The controllers of physical energy in the universes.

name: Master Physical Controllers
note: The mobilizers and directors of physical energies.

name: Constellation Fathers
note: The Vorondadek rulers of the constellations.

name: Twenty-four counselors
note: The council of twenty-four advisers on Jerusem.

name: Twelve apostles
note: The twelve men Jesus chose and ordained to preach the kingdom.

name: The seventy
note: The seventy evangelists ordained to assist the apostles.

name: Women's corps
note: The corps of women evangelists organized to minister to women.

name: Pharisees
note: A Jewish religious party prominent in the gospel narratives.

name: Sadducees
note: The priestly Jewish party at the time of Jesus.

name: Essenes
note: The separatist Jewish sect of Jesus' time.

name: Sanhedrin
note: The Jewish high court that tried Jesus.

name: Samaritans
note: The mixed people of Samaria, ministered to by Jesus.

name: Andonites
note: The descendants of Andon and Fonta, the first human race.

name: Nodites
note: The descendants of the Prince's staff, centered in the land of Nod.

name: Andites
note: The blended race of Adamites and Nodites that civilized Mesopotamia.

name: Sangik peoples
note: The six colored races that appeared in the Sangik family.

name: Violet race
note: The Adamic race, the violet people of Adam and Eve's line.

name: Adamites
note: The descendants of Adam, the violet race.

name: The Prince's staff
note: The one hundred Jerusem volunteers rematerialized to serve at Dalamatia.

name: Paradise
note: The eternal Isle at the center of all things, dwelling place of Deity.

name: Havona
note: The central universe of one billion perfect worlds surrounding Paradise.

name: Uversa
note: The capital of the superuniverse Orvonton.

name: Orvonton
note: The seventh superuniverse, containing the local universe Nebadon.

name: Salvington
note: The capital of the local universe Nebadon.

name: Nebadon
note: The local universe of Michael's creation, containing Urantia.

name: Satania
note: The administrative system containing Urantia, rebelled under Lucifer.

name: Jerusem
note: The capital of the system Satania.

name: Edentia
note: The capital of the constellation Norlatiadek.

name: Norlatiadek
note: The constellation containing the system Satania.

name: Urantia
note: The name of the planet Earth in universe records.

name: Dalamatia
note: The headquarters city of the Planetary Prince on Urantia.

name: Eden
note: The prepared garden home of Adam and Eve on Urantia.

name: Land of Nod
note: The region east of Eden settled by the Nodites.

name: Second Garden
note: The Adamic headquarters established after Eden.

name: Mansion worlds
note: The seven worlds where ascending mortals are repersonalized.

name: Jerusalem
note: The holy city of the Jews, scene of Jesus' death and resurrection.

name: Bethlehem
note: The city of David, birthplace of Jesus.

name: Nazareth
note: The Galilean town where Jesus grew up.

name: Capernaum
note: The lakeside city that became Jesus' headquarters in Galilee.

name: Galilee
note: The northern province where Jesus did most of his public work.

name: Judea
note: The southern Jewish province containing Jerusalem.

name: Samaria
note: The district between Judea and Galilee, home of the Samaritans.

name: Perea
note: The province east of the Jordan, scene of Jesus' later ministry.

name: Decapolis
note: The league of ten gentile cities east of Galilee.

name: Sea of Galilee
note: The lake at the center of Jesus' Galilean ministry.

name: Mount Olivet
note: The hill east of Jerusalem associated with Jesus' last days.

name: Gethsemane
note: The garden where Jesus prayed before his arrest.

name: Golgotha
note: The place of the crucifixion, outside Jerusalem.

name: Egypt
note: The ancient land prominent in Hebrew history and in Jesus' youth.

name: Rome
note: The imperial capital visited by Jesus on his Mediterranean tour.

name: Athens
note: The Greek city where Jesus reasoned with the philosophers.

name: Antioch
note: The Syrian city, later a center of gentile Christianity.

name: Alexandria
note: The Egyptian city visited on the Mediterranean tour.

name: Babylon
note: The Mesopotamian city of the Jewish captivity.

name: Persia
note: The eastern empire in the book's historical narratives.

name: India
note: The land of Gautama, later visited by Nathaniel.

name: China
note: The Far Eastern land discussed in the book's racial and religious history.

name: Mesopotamia
note: The land between the rivers, cradle of Dalamatia and Eden.

name: Tyre
note: The Phoenician city visited during Jesus' later ministry.

name: Sidon
note: The Phoenician city of Jesus' tour with the apostles.

name: Caesarea-Philippi
note: The northern city where Peter confessed Jesus as the Son of God.

name: Gennesaret
note: The plain on the Sea of Galilee where Jesus ministered.

name: Bethsaida
note: The fishing town, home of several apostles.

name: Cana
note: The Galilean town of the wedding feast attended by Jesus.

name: Magdala
note: The lakeside town associated with Mary Magdalene.

name: Tiberias
note: The Herodian capital on the Sea of Galilee.

name: Gadara
note: A city of the Decapolis visited by Jesus.

name: Sychar
note: The Samaritan town of Jacob's well.

name: Bethany
note: The village near Jerusalem, home of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary.

name: Emmaus
note: The village where the risen Jesus appeared to two believers.

name: Mount Hermon
note: The high mountain of the transfiguration.

name: Jordan River
note: The river where John baptized and Jesus began his public ministry.

name: Dead Sea
note: The salt sea at the Jordan's mouth.

name: Damascus
note: The Syrian city on Jesus' Mediterranean route.

name: Urmia
note: The Persian city where Jesus lectured on the kingdom.

name: Corinth
note: The Greek city visited on the Mediterranean tour.

name: Carthage
note: The North African city visited on the Mediterranean tour.

name: Cyrene
note: The North African city on the Mediterranean tour; Simon of Cyrene came from here.

name: Onamonalonton
note: Leader and spiritual deliverer of the red men who brought them temporary peace and turned them from many gods to worship of the Great Spirit.

name: Serapatatia
note: Brown-tinted leader of the Syrian Nodite confederation who allied his people with Adam and became an honest, sincere lieutenant unknowingly used by Caligastia.

name: Onagar
note: Master mind of the pre-Planetary Prince age who led and brought peace to the Andonic tribes and first united them in worship of the Breath Giver.

name: Orlandof
note: Prince and great teacher of the blue men who led many tribes back to worship of the true God as the Supreme Chief.

name: Porshunta
note: Oracle and master mind of the extinct orange race whose wise leadership brought a revival of higher living and worship of the Great Teacher.

name: Singlangton
note: First yellow man to lead his people in worship of the One Truth, whose lingering teachings persisted in the Chinese concept of Shang-ti.

name: Fantad
note: Deliverer of the green men from darkness, under whose leadership the green race experienced a great cultural revival and worshiped the One Source of Life.

name: Orvonon
note: Enlightener of the indigo races in Africa, under whom they experienced a great spiritual awakening and served the God of Gods.

name: Cano
note: Brilliant Nodite leader friendly to the Garden whose secret meeting with Eve made him the father of Cain; he perished when Edenites destroyed his settlement.

name: Ganid
note: Young son of Gonod from India, taught by Jesus during their Mediterranean tour, with whom he developed a great mutual affection.

name: Thor
note: Victorious commander of the northern armies in the final battle of the Somme, later a hero of the northern white tribes and revered by some as a god.

name: Sato
note: Direct descendant of Adamson and Ratta who led the tall Adamsonite progenitors of the Greeks westward over the northern islands to Greece.

name: Fad
note: Member of the Prince's staff who headed the educational faculty, formulated the first alphabet, and remained loyal during the rebellion.

name: Hap
note: Head of the college of revealed religion on the Prince's staff who provided Dalamatians with chants of worship and remained loyal in the rebellion.

name: Mek
note: Leader of the planetary council on art and science on the Prince's staff who advanced Andonite culture and improved the art of the blue man.

name: Lanaforge
note: Primary Lanonandek Son and System Sovereign of Satania succeeding Lucifer, previously proven loyal to Michael during an earlier system rebellion in Nebadon.

name: Manotia
note: Second in command of the Satania headquarters seraphim who refused to join the Lucifer rebellion and saved almost two thirds of the administrator angels.

name: Tabamantia
note: Agondonter finaliter and sovereign supervisor of the experimental worlds who inspected Urantia and recommended that it be granted Material Sons.

name: Solonia
note: Seraphic chief of the planetary helpers, the voice in the Garden, who proclaimed the miscarriage of the Adamic plan and presented narratives of Eden.

name: Father Melchizedek
note: Original Melchizedek of Nebadon, offspring of the Creator Son and Creative Spirit, who serves as Gabriel's first executive associate on Salvington.

name: Mantutia Melchizedek
note: Melchizedek who directed the Nebadon commission of twelve that sponsored and authorized a series of papers narrating the history of Urantia.

name: 1-2-3 the first
note: Eldest primary midwayer who stood with Van and Amadon during the rebellion, later serving as governor general and as one of the twenty-four counselors.

name: Beelzebub
note: Leader of the disloyal secondary midway creatures who allied themselves with the forces of Caligastia in the planetary rebellion.

name: Laotta
note: Brilliant Nodite woman heading the western schools of the Garden, with whom Adam deliberately shared Eve's folly; she died giving birth to Sansa.

name: Sansa
note: Daughter of Laotta, reared by Eve with Cain, who became a woman of great ability and wife of Sargan, aiding the advancement of the blue men.

name: Sargan
note: Chief of the northern blue races who married Sansa, the daughter of Laotta reared by Eve.

name: Enoch (Adjuster-fused mortal)
note: The first mortal of Urantia to fuse with the Thought Adjuster during life in the flesh.

name: Ikhnaton
note: Young Pharaoh of Egypt who accepted the Melchizedek doctrine of One God and methodically tried to swing his nation from polytheism to monotheism.

name: Zoroaster
note: Persian teacher of the sixth century before Christ who revived the Salem gospel and founded a religion centered on the one God.

name: Lao-tse
note: Outstanding Chinese teacher of great spiritual vision who built upon Salem traditions in declaring Tao the One First Cause of all creation.

name: Confucius
note: Younger contemporary of Lao in China who compiled the sayings of ancient philosophers and put morality in place of magic.

name: Elijah (prophet)
note: Fearless Hebrew prophet of the northern kingdom who overthrew the altars of Baal and, beginning as an agrarian reformer, ended by exalting Deity.

name: Amos
note: Hebrew prophet from the southern hills who discovered new concepts of Deity, proclaimed Yahweh God of all nations, and was stoned to death.

name: Hosea
note: Hebrew prophet who followed Amos, revived the Mosaic concept of a God of love, and preached forgiveness through repentance and divine mercy.

name: Isaiah (the first)
note: Hebrew prophet who preached the eternal nature of God, his infinite wisdom and his unchanging perfection of reliability.

name: Jeremiah
note: Intrepid Hebrew prophet who took the next step in internationalizing Yahweh, declaring him God of all nations and not partisan in Hebrew wars.

name: Isaiah the second
note: Young prophet of the Babylonian captivity, a convert to the elder Isaiah's God of love, whose teachings were incorporated in the book of Isaiah.

name: Daniel
note: Hebrew prophet who presented the drama of an impending crisis and the establishment of the Messianic kingdom; John the Baptist much favored his writings.

name: Rebecca (daughter of Ezra)
note: Eldest daughter of a Nazareth merchant who fell in love with the young Jesus, never married, and followed his ministry to the cross.

name: Zaccheus
note: Rich, short chief publican of Jericho who climbed a tree to see Jesus, hosted him, and pledged half his goods to the poor.

name: Annas
note: Former high priest and father-in-law of Caiaphas, the most powerful individual in Jewry, who conducted the preliminary examination of Jesus.

name: Alexander (Macedonian king)
note: Macedonian king who spread Hellenistic civilization over the near-Eastern world and permitted the Samaritans to build their temple on Mount Gerizim.

name: Genghis Khan
note: Leader under whom the Mongols began conquering most of Asia, the last great manifestation of the submerged military genius of the central Asiatic Andites.

name: Herod the Great
note: Idumean ruler who won overlordship of Judea by courting Rome, built temples to strange gods and the harbor of Caesarea; father of Herod Antipas.

name: Tiberius
note: Roman emperor who received Gonod, Ganid and Jesus in Rome and kept Pontius Pilate as procurator of Judea for ten years.

name: Mansant
note: Great teacher of the post-Planetary Prince age on Urantia who pointed his fellows to the veneration of the Great Light.

name: Rantowoc
note: Wise man of the red race of long ago, the first mortal on Urantia to secure a personal guardian of destiny.

name: Ellanora
note: Young woman of Panoptia who took the leadership of its human races during the Lucifer rebellion, so that none of her world joined the rebels.

name: Nabon
note: Greek Jew and leading high priest of the Mithraic cult in Rome, deeply influenced by talks with Jesus and later a help to gospel preachers.

name: Fortune
note: Youth who later became the leader of the Christians in Crete and a close associate of Titus in uplifting the Cretan believers.

name: Bon
note: Director of the board of animal domestication and utilization among the Prince's one hundred; his group trained the great fandors as passenger birds.

name: Lut
note: Leader of the guardians of health and life, the council on sanitation and hygiene; he and the whole board of health were lost in the rebellion.

name: Tut
note: Chief of the governors of advanced tribal relations, who worked to humanize warfare and improve tribal governments; he and his commission went astray in the rebellion.

name: Abel
note: First child of Adam and Eve born in the second garden, a herder who kept reminding Cain that Adam was not his father and was slain by him.

name: Cain
note: Son of Eve born before the Adamic caravan reached Mesopotamia; he slew Abel, went to the land of Nod and married Remona.

name: Sontad
note: First child of the first human pair, born wrapped in protective coverings, who led the clan after his parents died, aided by his wife.

name: Badonan
note: Great-great-grandson of Andon whose tribes in the northwestern Indian highlands kept a long-lasting center of culture and never practiced human sacrifice.

name: Bablot
note: Descendant of Nod who planned a temple and tower of racial glorification; the city named after him later became known as Babel.

name: Annan
note: Loyal daughter and spokesman for the Nodites on the twelve-member reception committee that welcomed Adam and Eve.

name: Remona
note: Distant cousin whom Cain married in the land of Nod; their first son, Enoch, became head of the Elamite Nodites.

name: Susanna (daughter of the Nazareth chazan)
note: Daughter of the former chazan of the Nazareth synagogue, one of the ten women commissioned by Jesus and elected chief of the women's group.

name: Joanna
note: Wife of Chuza, steward of Herod Antipas; one of the ten women commissioned by Jesus and elected their treasurer.

name: Celta
note: Daughter of a Roman centurion, one of the ten women Jesus commissioned for the ministering work of the kingdom.

name: Agaman
note: Widow of Damascus, one of the ten women Jesus commissioned for the ministering work of the kingdom.

name: Nasanta
note: Daughter of Elman the Syrian physician, one of the ten women Jesus commissioned for the ministering work of the kingdom.

name: Milcha
note: Cousin of the Apostle Thomas, one of the ten women Jesus commissioned for the ministering work of the kingdom.

name: Rachel (sister-in-law of Jude)
note: Sister-in-law of Jude, one of the women evangelists; she helped win Mary Magdalene and asked Jesus what to tell women seeking salvation.

name: Ruth (daughter of Matthew Levi)
note: Eldest daughter of Matthew Levi, one of the ten women Jesus commissioned for the ministering work of the kingdom.

name: Seth
note: Eldest surviving son of Adam and Eve born in the second garden, who became head of its new priesthood; father of Enos.

name: Rebecca (daughter of Joseph of Arimathea)
note: Daughter of Joseph of Arimathea, added by Jesus to the women evangelists and set apart for service with Mary Magdalene at Jotapata.

name: Malavatia Melchizedek
note: Melchizedek named as the sponsor of the paper on the constellations.

name: Mansurotia
note: Tertiary Lanonandek who serves as first assistant Sovereign of Satania, sent to the system along with Lanaforge.

name: Holdant
note: Tertiary Lanonandek who is custodian of the Satania system, holder of interned spirits above mortal order; he came with Lanaforge.

name: Hanavard
note: Primary Lanonandek and high counselor who acts as chairman of the executive council of Satania on Jerusem.

name: Gavalia
note: First-born and head of the Brilliant Evening Stars of Nebadon, assigned to ascendant mortal ministry, who presented the story of Michael's bestowals.

name: Galantia
note: Associate of Gavalia with headquarters on Jerusem, the first ascendant superangel commissioned as a Brilliant Evening Star.

name: Grandfanda
note: First of all mortals to attain Havona, a pilgrim from a distant superuniverse whose arrival inaugurated the broadcasts of the universe of universes.

name: Malvorian
note: First of the Graduate Guides, chief of their supreme council, who greeted the first mortal pilgrim and guided him through Havona.

name: Faithful of Days (of Edentia)
note: Trinity Son of Paradise on Edentia, personal representative of Immanuel, who counsels the Constellation Fathers only when asked.

name: Jacob (son of the stone mason)
note: Neighbor boy and self-appointed defender of the young Jesus, later a stone mason and business associate of James and Joseph who sought Miriam in marriage.

name: Miriam (sister of Jesus)
note: Sister of Jesus, a level-headed daughter and belle of the family, whose marriage to Jacob the stone mason Jesus blessed.

name: Hannah (mother of Mary)
note: Wife of Joachim and mother of Mary; she and her family were skeptical about the divine mission of Jesus.

name: Elijah Mark
note: Father of John Mark and staunch friend of the apostles, at whose Jerusalem home the Last Supper was held; he died suddenly of a brain hemorrhage.

name: Mary Mark
note: Woman whose Jerusalem home, shared with Elijah Mark, housed the apostles in its upper chamber and hosted a gathering of foremost disciples.

name: Gadiah
note: A young Philistine interpreter at Joppa who became a warm friend of Jesus, later a profound believer, and influenced Simon the leather merchant to embrace Christianity.

name: Claudia Procula
note: Wife of Pilate who learned of Jesus through her Phoenician maid-in-waiting, sent Pilate a sealed message during the trial, and later helped spread the gospel.

name: Mangus
note: A Roman centurion at Capernaum who built the local synagogue and asked the Jewish elders to beseech Jesus to heal his dying servant.

name: Norana
note: A Syrian woman who brought her afflicted daughter to Jesus for healing; her humor and persistent faith deeply touched the Master.

name: Nalda
note: A Samaritan woman of Sychar who talked with Jesus at Jacob’s well about living water and worship, and to whom he later appeared after the resurrection.

name: Samuel
note: A Hebrew prophet and practical reformer from a line of Salem teachers who sought to turn Israel back to the worship of the supreme Yahweh.

name: Saul (king of Israel)
note: A Hebrew leader who defeated the Ammonites and was then made king by popular election of his troops, without any priest or prophet participating.

name: Solomon
note: Son of Bathsheba and successor of David who continued his father’s tyranny and taxation and bankrupted the nation with a lavish court and building program.

name: Noah (wine maker of Aram)
note: A wine maker of Aram near Erech who warned of yearly floods and was saved with his family in a houseboat when a great flood destroyed his village.

name: Job
note: The prosperous servant of the Lord in the Scripture parable of affliction, who challenged the doctrine that God afflicts children to punish their parents.

name: Elisha
note: The faithful associate of Elijah who took up his work and, with Micaiah, kept the light of truth alive in Palestine.

name: Deborah
note: A woman who ruled the Hebrews and, with Barak, defeated Sisera at Taanach; her general showed no mercy to the defeated gentiles.

name: Ahab
note: King of Ephraim who resisted Shalmaneser III at Karkar and was denounced by Elijah for the murder of Naboth in the scheme to obtain his land.

name: Josiah (king of Judah)
note: A king of Judah under whom the country folk destroyed the corrupt Jerusalem political ring, until he was wiped out intercepting the army of Necho.

name: Hagar
note: A concubine of Abraham, named in a passage noting that Keturah likewise was merely a concubine and not a wife.

name: Katro
note: Head of the family with whom Melchizedek lived for more than thirty years; the family long preserved his teachings down to their descendant Moses.

name: Amdon
note: A Chaldean herder of Sumerian extraction, the first mortal to observe Machiventa Melchizedek, who announced his mission in Amdon’s tent.

name: Jaram the Hittite
note: A student of Melchizedek sent to invite Abraham and Nahor to come to Salem to hear the teachings of the eternal Creator.

name: Absalom
note: A figure in the rebellion that broke out against David’s corrupt regime, whom the book likens to a modern demagogue; his mother was a Canaanite.

name: Stephen
note: A young Hellenist who once talked with Jesus in Jerusalem, later led the Greek believers there, and was stoned as the first martyr of the new faith.

name: Barnabas
note: An able Greek in Jerusalem who, with Stephen, was among the early Hellenist converts made by two pupils of Rodan.

name: Flavius
note: A Greek Jew and lover of art at whose Jerusalem home Jesus often stayed and met inquirers, and where he later appeared to Greek believers.

name: Matadormus
note: A rich young Pharisee of the Jerusalem Sanhedrin who sought ordination but went away sorrowful when asked to part with his possessions.

name: Gamaliel
note: One of the leading rabbis of Jerusalem, whose counsel to leave the followers of Jesus alone brought a time of peace to the early believers.

name: Plato
note: A Greek philosopher, successor of Socrates, who taught that virtue is knowledge; the book compares his place in Greek philosophy with Confucius in Chinese morality.

name: Socrates
note: A Greek philosopher who, with his successors Plato and Aristotle, taught that virtue is knowledge and that it is wrong to return evil for evil.

name: Aristotle
note: A Greek philosopher, successor of Socrates and Plato, who shared their teaching that virtue is knowledge and goodness is health of the soul.

name: Anaxagoras
note: A Greek thinker described as a mechanist except that he recognized a First Cause, an Initial Mind.

name: Amenemope
note: An Egyptian teacher who exalted conscience and passed on ethics and morals to Hebrews and Greeks; parts of Proverbs derive from his Book of Wisdom.

name: Frandalanks
note: The most numerous order of Master Physical Controllers, jointly created by force organizers and power directors and stationed on all inhabited worlds.

name: Energy Transformers
note: An order of Master Physical Controllers created by the Supreme Power Directors and Center Supervisors, usually one hundred per inhabited world.

name: Associate Power Directors
note: An order of Master Physical Controllers that assigns and dispatches the physical controllers according to the changing energy needs of the realms.

name: Seven Supreme Power Directors
note: The seven physical-energy regulators of the grand universe, created by the Seven Master Spirits, each in eternal union with one Master Spirit.

name: Personalized Adjusters
note: Thought Adjusters granted personality by the Universal Father after experience with mortals, classed as the highest order of ascending Sons of God.

name: Foxhall peoples
note: Andonite tribes who were the first humans in England, retaining much Andonic culture and flintworking, and ancestors of the Eskimos.

name: Heidelberg race
note: A somewhat superior and prolific people whose descendants spread over Europe from the northern ice to the Alps and the Mediterranean.

name: Neanderthal race
note: A people descended from improved Badonite stock; excellent fighters who spread from northwest India to France, China and northern Africa and long dominated the world.

name: Indigo race
note: The last and least progressive of the six Sangik races, who migrated to Africa and later experienced a great spiritual awakening under Orvonon.

name: Dawn mammals
note: Small, agile, flesh-eating prehuman creatures descended from the North American lemur type, which suddenly appeared in Mesopotamia and developed a strong tribal spirit.

name: Mid-mammals
note: The prehuman species founded by superior twins born to dawn mammals, improved in every way over their ancestors and showing several rudimentary human traits.

name: Primates
note: The prehuman species founded by superior twins born to mid-mammal parents, who walked erect from birth; the direct animal ancestors of the human family.

name: Bartimeus
note: An elderly beggar at Jericho, blind from his youth, whose sight Jesus restored in response to his faith.

name: Veronica
note: A woman of Caesarea-Philippi whose faith healed her of a malady when she approached Jesus; he corrected her belief that touching his garment had cured her.

name: Malchus
note: The Syrian bodyguard of the high priest who moved to bind Jesus at his arrest, provoking Peter to draw his sword.

name: Eber
note: The Sanhedrin officer sent to arrest Jesus at the temple, who refused to do so and defended him before the chief priests and Pharisees.

name: Imhotep
note: An Andite architectural genius who, while serving as prime minister, erected the first and most exquisite of the stone pyramids in Egypt.

name: Amosad
note: The leader under whom the Sethite priesthood was regenerated, inaugurating a brilliant era in the culture of the second garden.

name: Hammurabi
note: An ancient Mesopotamian ruler who recognized punishment by burning; by the time of his rule the Sumerians had been absorbed by the northern Semites.

name: Unions of Days
note: Trinity-origin liaison personalities, one assigned to each local universe as counselor and representative of the Paradise Trinity to its rulers.

name: Universal Censors
note: Trinity-origin beings who are the judgment of Deity, rendering verdicts in liaison with Perfectors of Wisdom and Divine Counselors.

name: Divine Counselors
note: Trinity-origin beings who are the counsel of Deity to the seven superuniverses, three billion being assigned to each.

name: Perfectors of Wisdom
note: A specialized creation of the Paradise Trinity personifying the wisdom of divinity, one billion assigned to each of the seven superuniverses.

name: Abaddon
note: The chief of staff of Caligastia, who followed him into rebellion and has since acted as chief executive of the Urantia rebels.

name: Elizabeth (mother of John the Baptist)
note: The wife of Zacharias and mother of John the Baptist, of the same family group as Mary, to whom Gabriel appeared to announce her son.

name: Anna (poetess of the temple)
note: A Galilean poetess of the temple courts, companion of Simeon and intimate of Zacharias, who wrote the hymn Simeon sang at the presentation of Jesus.

name: Matthias
note: The man chosen by lot to take the place of Judas as an apostle, who served as treasurer but took little part in later apostolic activities.

name: Hildana
note: The woman brought before Jesus as an adulteress, whom he refused to condemn; she left her wicked husband and joined the disciples.

name: Jairus
note: A ruler of the Capernaum synagogue whose daughter Jesus raised; he later resigned as chief ruler and openly aligned himself with Jesus.

name: Cymboyton
note: A wealthy merchant of Urmia who with his three sons built and presided over a school of religion, never revealing his own beliefs.

name: Anaxand
note: A young Greek shipyard worker at Caesarea taught by Jesus, who later became a believer, a steward of Cornelius, and a minister to the suffering.

name: Karuska
note: A woman at whose home Jesus lodged seeking rest; her servant told the neighboring Syrian mother Norana of his presence there.

name: Mardus
note: The acknowledged leader of the Cynics of Rome, who befriended Jesus and conversed with him daily, notably about good and evil.

name: Elihu
note: The prophet of Ur and priest of the Salem believers, whose teaching proclaimed salvation by faith and divine favor.

name: Godad
note: A hermit of India, descended from a family that kept the Melchizedek missionary traditions, whose instruction Gautama did not heed.

name: Kenan
note: The grandson of Seth, who instituted the foreign missionary service of the second garden to the surrounding tribes.

name: Enos
note: The son of Seth, who founded the new order of worship of the second garden.

name: Jansad
note: The eldest son of Eveson, who became the successor of Adam as head of the Adamite tribes.

name: Zacharias
note: A Jewish priest, husband of Elizabeth and father of John the Baptist, who was long skeptical of Gabriel's announcement of his son.

name: Cedes
note: A believer at Antioch who made a brief record that Luke used as one of the sources for his Gospel.
